# dsh-plugin-forge-cnb
English | 中文

CNB (cnb.cool) provider for the DSH **forge registry**. It registers a
`ForgeProvider` with `ctx.for

ge`, so the change request and working tree panel can show CNB merge
requests: state, additions/dele

tions, mergeability, checks, reviewers, diff, file contents, review
publication, and merge.
This is a host-side bundle with **zero runtime dependencies**: global `fetch` and Node built-ins onl

y,
Node.js >= 22. No client or DSH package change is needed — registering the provider is enough.
## What it adds
| contract method | CNB source |
| `repositoryFromRemote` / `changeRequestFromUrl` / `changeRequestUrl` | remote-URL and MR-URL parsi
ng for `https`, `ssh://`, and scp-like remotes, nested groups (`a/b/c`), `.git` suffixes, ports; the

two URL functions are exact inverses |
| `fetch` | `GET /{repo}/-/pulls/{n}` + `GET /{repo}/-/pulls
/{n}/commit-statuses`, plus per-head-commit totals (`…/files`), head commit date (`…/git/commits/{sh

a}`), and cached repository merge settings |
| `fetchChecks` | the same reads, always with the compl

ete check list (no 50-row polling cap) |
| `findByHead` | `GET /{repo}/-/pulls?state=open&page_size=

100&page=N`, filtered client-side (CNB has no head-branch filter) |
| `diff` | `GET /{repo}/-/pulls/

{n}/files`, assembled into one Git-style unified patch |
| `fileText` / `fileUrl` | `GET /{repo}/-/g
it/raw/{commit}/{path}` (falls back to the base64 contents endpoint on HTTP 413), and the `/-/blob/{

commit}/{path}` web URL |
| `merge` | re-reads the MR, compares `head.sha` with the confirmed commit

, then `PUT /{repo}/-/pulls/{n}/merge` with `merge_style`; never sends `force` |
| `markReady` | no

API exists; returns a clear failure telling the user to edit the WIP title in the web UI |
| `submit

Review` | `POST /{repo}/-/pulls/{n}/reviews` with `event` and inline `comments` |
| `readiness` | `G
ET /user`; an expired or missing token reads as `unauthenticated` and tells the user to run `cnb log
ser`; an expired or missing token reads as `unauthenticated` and tells the user to run `cnb login` |
## Install
This is a DSH bundle distributed from GitHub rather than npm. Clone it, then install the checked-out
directory as a bundle in your profile (for example with the Plugin Manager's install-bundle flow, o

r the
`plugin_manager` tool with `action: install_bundle`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bundle ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the provider row; you pick the bundle, no

t the
row. It needs Node.js >= 22 on the host and a valid `cnb login` session (`~/.cnb/token`, re-re

ad whenever
the CLI refreshes it).
## Enable it
The bundle ships a Cordis patch, so enabling it in the profile is one entry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| config field | default | meaning |
| `hosts` | `['cnb.cool']` | web hosts this provider serves; repositories on other hosts are ignored

|
| `tokenFile` | `~/.cnb/token` | CNB CLI credential file; `CNB_TOKEN` in the environment override

s it |
| `timeoutMs` | `10000` | deadline of one HTTP request, combined with the caller's cancellati

on |
| `maxPages` | `3` | pages of 100 open MRs `findByHead` reads per lookup |
Nothing is written to any repository unless you explicitly merge or submit a review.
## How a merge request binds to a session

The forge session layer discovers a session's change request by running `git` in the session
checkou

t: it maps the checkout's remote to a repository (`repositoryFromRemote`) and then asks
`findByHead(

repository, branch)` for open MRs whose **head** is the current branch. Pasting a CNB MR URL
into th

e session binds it directly (`changeRequestFromUrl`), and bindings are re-resolved through
`changeRe
questUrl` → `changeRequestFromUrl`, which is why those two are exact inverses.
`gh` command output parsing does **not** apply here — that is GitHub-CLI specific. For CNB the only
binding paths are the git remote/branch discovery and a pasted MR URL.

## Known limitations
- **WIP cannot be cleared through the API**: `is_wip` is read-only on CNB, so `markReady` always fai

ls with
a message asking the user to edit the title in the web UI. The provider never PATCHes the ti

tle.
- **The changed-file list is hard-capped at 300 entries** even though CNB documents it as unpag

inated
(a verified 490-file MR returns 300). `additions`/`deletions` and `diff()` therefore cover at

most 300
files for a very large MR; there is no truncation flag to expose and no workaround endpoin

t.
- **Rename origin is not recoverable** from the MR file list; a rename renders as a change of the

new path
(no `rename from` header) unless the payload happens to carry `previous_filename`. Only
`G

ET /{repo}/-/git/compare/{base}...{head}` exposes it, and that endpoint shares the 300-file cap.
- *
*No close/merge timestamp** (see `closedAt`), so the panel cannot show when an MR was merged or clos

ed.
- **Resolve state of review threads is unavailable** (see `unresolvedThreads`).
- **Merge refusa

l shape is unverified**: CNB documents `403` (`die.WebError`) but may answer `200` with
`merged:fals

e`; both are handled as `failed` with the host message. `fast_forward` is a valid CNB
`merge_style`

but not part of the forge contract's method set, so it is not offered.
- **Fork merge requests**: CN

B bakes the *base* repository path plus the head commit into the file URLs,
and the base repository

refuses a raw read of a foreign commit (HTTP 400 `errcode 3`). The provider
detects a fork via `head

.repo.id !== base.repo.id` (or differing paths), caches the head repository per
change request, and

reads `fileText`/`fileUrl` from `head.repo.path`. Before the first poll it learns the
head repositor

y from one MR detail read when the base read fails.
- **The diff/hunks are whatever the host returns

**: this provider does not re-number hunks or trim lines,
because a count mismatch would make the pa

nel's parser throw.
- **Custom hosts**: only `cnb.cool` is tested; for another host the API base is

derived as
`https://api.<host>` and the token must exist under that host key in the token file.
